subject: Simplify stan::lang::compile by throwing exceptions on errors

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Simplify stan::lang::compile by throwing exceptions on errors
parts:
Hi,

It would be great for interface writers if errors were standardized. If
we're going to throw exceptions when some "invalid" data is passed to a
function, we should always try to throw exceptions.

One case where something in-between is happening is stan::lang::compile
and I wonder if it couldn't be simplified by just throwing exceptions
when there is a parse error or an error in generating the cpp code.

For example, it seems like we're going to throw errors in the var_context
refactor; here's a bit of Michael's code which throws an exception
when someone passes an invalid `name` to a function:

> std::vector<size_t> dims = dims_r(name);
> if (dims.size() != 1) {
> std::stringstream msg;
> msg << "Requested the vector " << name
> << ", but " << name
> << " is not defined as a vector in variable context"
> << std::endl;
> throw std::runtime_error(msg.str());
> }

Could we simplify ``stan::lang::compile`` by throwing
std::runtime_error`s? Here's the current signature

bool compile(std::ostream* msgs,
std::istream& stan_lang_in,
std::ostream& cpp_out,
const std::string& model_name,
const std::string& in_file_name = "input") {

Could we do something like this instead, returning ``cpp_out``.

std::string compile(std::string stan_lang_in, const std::string& model_name)

and rely on exceptions to communicate parsing and generator errors?

Packing several parsing errors into an exception doesn't seem so bad to
me -- I think we have lengthy exception error messages elsewhere. If it
is a bad idea then could we standardize what we should do in this kind
of case? Like create a simple struct which encapsulates the possible
results and which could be used in other cases? Here's what compile
could return instead, which would be closer to the existing setup:

struct StanStringResult {
int error; // 0 or 1
std::string error_msg;
std::string result;
} StanResult;

(The current signature for stan::lang::compile also looks a little like
a cmdstand-ism lurking in Stan).

If there's interest in this change, I'm willing to work on it as part of
the overall refactor effort.

Best,

Allen

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Simplify stan::lang::compile by throwing exceptions on errors
parts:
What's happening under the hood is that the stream's
getting plumbed through the parser so that each semantic
action on a rule (for instance, the sampling statement
rule) can write to the stream.

The way to make this more structured isn't to continue
to write to the stream and add a flag, it's to return
a structured set of warnings.

I'm still not clear on why you want to change the behavior
with stanc. Who's going to catch these exceptions and what
are they going to do with them? That's always the place to
start with exception design.

Right now, there's two ways to fail. You can either get
an exception in the code when there's a failed expectation
(such as an opening brace without the expected close brace)
and a parse failure when the program's ill formed for other
reasons. This is just the behavior inherited from the Spirit
Qi parser, but we could always take a negative return and
throw an exception.

The compile method in stan::lang::compile() is the top level call.
You can see that it gets a boolean return from the underlying
Spirit Qi parser, and it just returns it if it's false. Otherwise,
it generates the C++, which can't fail and returns true.

If you then look at stan::lang::parse(), which is called by the
compiler, you can see the try/catch blocks where the errors
are trapped and written rather than rethrown. The reason
for that is that there's nothing higher-level to catch them.

Would you rather that functionality moved up to the calling
program, which could catch an exception?

- Bob

Yes, I was thinking that we might consider having the calling program
catch the exception since that's what we seem to be doing elsewhere.

In general, I think it would be good if stan::lang::compile could accept
a simpler set of params and return a tidy object. This seems like it
would be in the spirit of the refactor and it would make wrapping
stan::lang::compile quite a bit easier.

Are you happy with the stan::lang::compile interface as it is?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Simplify stan::lang::compile by throwing exceptions on errors
parts:
What we have now is fine for CmdStan, but I can't speak for
the other interfaces. I'm sure CmdStan would be easy to
modify for whatever we decide.

The Stan 3 command refactor has the interfaces pass in
callbacks for I/O. This allows consistent behavior
across interfaces, which is my main goal along with removing
code duplication.

I don't like the idea of having the interfaces catch the
exceptions and deal with them as it will neither reduce
code duplication nor encourage consistent behavior across interfaces.

Right now, we have a callback structure for the interfaces,
but the callback is a simple output stream. It would be a
lot of work, but straightforward to change the parser API to pass
in a structured callback handler for warnings, errors, etc.

So the question is what should it do?

For example, how much logger-like behavior do you want?
Loggers often configure messages to have log levels, like
fatal error, recoverable error, warning, debug (very verbose mode), etc.
Here's the spec for log4j:

https://logging.apache.org/log4j/1.2/apidocs/org/apache/log4j/Level.html

Then there's the issue of formatting the output --- do you include
thread IDs, time stamps, etc. And then there's the issue of how a user
or programmatic client configures the logger and where it pipes output.

- Bob

P.S. I don't like big heterogeneous data structures for returns.
For example, I don't like the return for R's built-in lm() function,
because it's mutable in such a way that allows it to get into
inconsistent states (models mismatching data mismatching estimates).
There are ways to mitigate these problems, but I think the callback
route is much cleaner. And it allows streaming.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Simplify stan::lang::compile by throwing exceptions on errors
parts:
The Stan 3 command refactor has the interfaces pass in callbacks
for I/O. This allows consistent behavior

across interfaces, which is my goal.

Your suggestion to throw exceptions and have the interfaces
deal with it will allow each interface to go its own way in
config and reporting, which is what we're trying to avoid (though
perhaps in vain).

Right now, we have that callback structure for the interfaces,
but the callback is a simple output stream. It would be possible
to change that API to have the interfaces pass in a structured
callback handler for warnings, errors, etc.
As far as being happy with what we currently have, it's fine
for CmdStan, but I can't speak for the other interfaces.

I'm sure it'll be easy for CmdStan to adapt to whatever changes
make sense for Python or R.

Refactoring the whole parsing interface to pass in a callback
handler for errors is a lot of work, but I think it would all be
straightforward. So the thing to do still is figure out what
the callback would be.

I don't think returning a big structure is the right
thing to do. It's a classic example of a "god object", like
the fit object in RStan, which I also don't like at all. It's
a despised anti-pattern in the OO community.
See, e.g., https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_object

So I'd rather stick to callbacks for a presentation layer.
If we do go with something like callbacks, there's the issue of how
much logger-like behavior we want. Loggers often configure

messages to have log levels, like fatal error, recoverable error,
warning, debug (very verbose mode), etc.
Here's the spec for log4j:

https://logging.apache.org/log4j/1.2/apidocs/org/apache/log4j/Level.html

Then there's the issue of formatting the output --- do you include
